SHERIFF’S SALE— By virtue of a writ of
Fieri Facias, issued out of the Court of Appeals
for the Western Shore of the State of Maryland to the
Sheriff of Baltimore County directed, at the suit of
Robert Robinson and Thomas Robinson, against the
goods and chattels, lands and tenements of Robert
Armstrong—I have seized and taken in execution, all
the estate, right, title, interest, property, claim and demand at law and inequity of the said Robert Arm
strong, in and to one Negro man named Daniel, aged
about twenty five years, a slave for life; one Negro
women aged about forty years, a slave for life;
one Negro girl aged about seventeen years, a slave
for life—Also, thirty shares of Baltimore Shot Tower
Stock, one Barouche, cover and harness, one sideboard, book case, one sofa, mahogany tables, 22

looking glasses, stair carpet, stair rods, bureaus, dressing glasses, 2 globes, a bag of feathers, three beds,
bedsteads and bedding, a lot of kitchen furniture, one
horse, one dray, &c.
And I hereby give notice, That on FRIDAY, the
19th day of June next at 10 o’clock, in the forenoon,
at the Court House, I will offer for sale the said property so seized and taken in execution, by Public auction to the highest bidder, for cash; and on Saturday
the 20th day of June next, at 10 o’clock, A. M. I will sell at the Soap and Candle Factory of the said Robert
Armstrong, in Concord street for cash, 3 copper soap
pans; I iron soap pan; 1 stove, &c.; 1 reel; 6 key tubs;
8 soap frames; moulds, stands, kettles, pans, and all
the fixtures attached to said Factory, and one wheelbarrow.

Court of Dorchester County, will he
sold at public sale, at Hicksburg, on Thursday, the 12th of February next, on a credit

to serve a term of years, and her two children, one and two years old, for life. They

purchasers, will moreover be required to give
bond that they shall not be disposed of to a
foreign purchaser or even removed from
the county.

Adm'x. of Mary S. J. B Vane, deceased.
Jan. 24 3w*
Notes: Silvia to be sold to serve a term of years and her two children for life. They will not be sold out of the county or to a foreign purchaser. Elizabeth H. Vane is the administrator of Mary S. J. B. Vane, dec'd.

Cash! Cash!! Cash!!
TO SLAVE OWNERS.
We have returned from the
South, and are again in the
market with a plentiful supply
of the needful, which we
will exchange for every description of negroes, old
and young either slaves for life or for a
term of years, whose owners have good
titles to them, and as it is usual for us to
do at all times we will pay higher prices
than any other person will do; we can at
all times be found here ready to purchase
any number. Persons having negroes for
sale who do not want them to go out at
the State may be assured that any negro
we buy under a promise not to send it out
of the Slate, in no event whatever, will it
be done. All persons who have negroes
for sale, and that want the highest prices
for them will please give us a call, and
they shall have it. All letters post paid,
not otherwise, will be promptly attended to.
JOHN N. DENNING & Co.
Centreville, 
Dec. 7, 1844.
Notes: John N. Denning & Co. looking to purchase slaves for life or a term of years after returning from the South. Will not sell slave out of state if owner should wish it. Ad repeated on May 24

WAKEFIELD FOR SALE.
I OFFER for sale, one of the best estates on the
Potomac River, containing about 1320 acres, between six and eight hundred of which are arable, and
now in cultivation. The land is generally a rich black
loam, interspersed with shells; and in fertility, is certainly equal, if not superior to any on the river. In
one of the fields, convenient to wood, is an inexhaustible bed of oyster shells, which could be easily converted into lime, and made useful on such parts of the
estate, as may not be already sufficiently supplied
with that valuable manure.
The BUILDINGS consist of an Overseer‘s
HOUSE, Granary, and all the outhouses necessary for the use of the Farm.
The estate is bounded on three sides, by Bridge
Creek, the River, and Pope’s Creek—requiring less
than the usual quantity of fencing to enclose it. It is
the birth place of Washington. Fish, Oysters and
Wild Fowl, are abundant, and indeed all the facilities
of living, are cheap and easily procured.
With the estate, I wish to dispose of from 18 to 20
LIKELY NEGROES, consisting of a fair proportion
of Men, Women, Boys and Children.
The health of the situation, may be estimated by the
fact, of which l am informed, that the physician’s bill,
for the last ten years has not averaged $10 per annum.
Society is good, and the neighborhood generally
healthy. If the number of very old persons, now living, and the bills of mortality were consulted, it would
be found to bear; a fair comparison with any of the
mountain regions of the State—indeed it is believed,
that in the last ten years, in proportion to population,
fewer deaths have occurred than in any other part of
Virginia. Apply at the office of the American.
The National Intelligencer, Washington, and the
Enquirer, Richmond, will publish the above.

PUBLIC SALE
OF LARGE AND  VERY VALUABLE REAL AND PERSONAL ESTATE
The undersigned will offer at public sale on WEDNESDAY, the 2nd day of APRIL next, on the premises, all that REAL ESTATE lying in Charles county, Maryland, called and known by the name of
"GLASVAR"
This estate contains about TWELVE HUNDRED Acres, and has been recently surveyed and laid off
into FOUR FARMS. The soil is equal to any in the county, and is now in a very highly improved condition--every part of the arable land having been heavily limed and manured. It is now capable of producing large and heavy crops of TOBACCO, CORN, WHEAT, OATS, &c., and from its proximity to navigable waters, (lying on the Wicomico, and being only one-and-a-half mile from the Potomac.) offers a most desirable and rare opportunity for those who wish to purchase real estate. It has upon it large and commodious BARNS and all the necessary QUARTERS and OUT-HOUSES, and an abundance of TIMBER and WOOD of the  very best kind. This estate will be sold in four separate parts, it having been divided into four farms of nearly the same size with a proportion of the buildings and wood on each. Those desirous of examining for themselves will be shown the place at any time by Mr. MURPHY, who is residing upon the premises, and all information given, in reference thereto, that may be desired, by either of the subscribers.
Also, at the same time, the VILLAGE adjoining, called and known by the name of-- 
ALLEN'S FRESH.
It contains a STORE-HOUSE with a DWELLING attached, and is one of the best locations for a Store tn this section of the State, being in the midst of a rich surrounding country, and the annual sale of goods there, it is believed, now reaches thirty-five or forty thousand dollars. There are also here three comfortable Dwellings, two Barns, and three Shops--all in good condition. Also, a
LARGE STEAM MILL,
for grinding Corn, Wheat, &c., in good repair and
now in operation. This village is situated on the head waters of the Wicomico, and goods may be landed within two hundred yards of the Store-House.
The undersigned will also sell at the same time and place a large amount of Personal Property, consisting of about One Hundred HORNED CATTLE, One Hundred SHEEP, a large number of HOGS, three pair of very superior MULES, HORSES, WAGONS, CARTS and FARMING UTENSILS of the various kinds used in the cultivation of an extensive farm.
THE TERMS OF SALE are as follows:-Upon the Real Estate one-fourth of the purchase money will be required in advance, and on the residue a credit will be given of twelve, eighteen and twenty-four months. For all purchases of Personal Property of thirty dollars and under the cash will be requied, and for all sums over that amount a credit of six months will be given. In every case where a credit if given the purchaser will be required to give bond for the amount, with such security as the undersigned will approve, bearing interest from the day of sale.
The above sale will commence at ten o'clock, A.M.
GEORGE BRENT,
R. T. MERRICK.
PORT TOBACCO, Feb. 26, 1851.

or trust, executed by George Thomas on the 4th day of
December, 1854. and recorded among the land records of St.
Mary's county, the subscriber. as trustee, will se!l on the
premises, at 10 o’clock, on THURSDAY , the 30th of April
(if fair. if not, the next fair day thereafter) a TRACT OF
LAND, lying on the Wycomico river, near Chaptico, St., 
Mary’s county. Md., commonly known as "Bashford," contalning TWO HUNDRED AND EIGHTY ACRES, more or
less. The said tract of land is located immediately upon the
river, with easy access to the markets of Baltimore, Washington and Alexandria by steamboats and by sail vessels.
The land is fertile and is particularly adapted to the growth
of tobacco of the finest texture.
The Wycomico, on which this farm is situated, furnishes
oystery, fish and wild fowl in abundance and perfection.
The improvements area BRICK DWELLING, containing
seven rooms, kitchen, work house, quarters, granaries, stables, carriage house, ice house, now filled with the ice, over-
seer’s house and three tobacco houses There is a pump of
fine water in the yard. A sufficient number of tobacco beds
have been seeded for the use of the farm, and if practicable,
the corn will be planted, and the manure, which is sufficient
to cover fifteen acres of land, will be applied and ploughed in
before the day of sale, and all other work will regularly progress with the season.
Ninety-eight bushels of Wheat were sown on this farm last
fall, which will be sold separately.
Terms of sale—One-fourth cash, and the balance in three
equal installments, payable in one, three and five years from
the day of sale, the purchaser giving bond with security to
be approved by the trustee, the said bonds bearing interest,
payable annually, from the day of sale.
Upon the receipt of the cash payment, and the other terms
of sale having been complied with, a deed will be given by
the trustee to the purchaser, and a mortgage will be taken
upon the land for the deferred payments and the annual payments of the interest.
